title: On the largest size of sum-free sets in symmetric regions
summary: A subset $S$ of a group $G$ is said to be sum-free (resp. $Δ$-free) if there are no solutions to $a+b=c$ (resp. $a+b+c=0$) with $a,b,c\in S$. For a convex region $R\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, let $σ(R)$ denote the maximal proportion of the volume of $R$ that a sum-free subset of $R$ can occupy. We prove that $σ([-1,1]^d)=1/2$. Our proof employs a careful application of the Brunn-Minkowski inequality. Moreover, for the $d$-dimensional Euclidean ball $\mathbb{B}^d(0,1)$, we show that $σ(\mathbb{B}^d(0,1))\leq 1/2+o_d(1)$.
